description: The bar chart titled “Model Evaluation on Academic and Practical Benchmarks” visually compares the performance of two language models — LLaMA-3-8B-it (blue bars) and Ours (Iterative RLHF) (orange bars) — across nine distinct evaluation datasets and metrics, displayed along the horizontal axis in the order: GSM-8K, MMLU, HumanEval, TruthfulQA, ARC, MBPP, LC AlpacaEval-2, MT-Bench (×5), and Chat-Arena-Hard. The vertical axis, labeled “Score (%)”, uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 80, with major tick marks at 10% intervals. On GSM-8K, both models achieve near-identical high scores, with LLaMA-3-8B-it at approximately 79% and Ours (Iterative RLHF) at 80%. For MMLU, LLaMA-3-8B-it scores around 66%, slightly higher than Ours (Iterative RLHF) at 65%. In HumanEval, Ours (Iterative RLHF) significantly outperforms with a score of 65%, compared to LLaMA-3-8B-it’s 61%. TruthfulQA shows a clear advantage for Ours (Iterative RLHF) at 60%, while LLaMA-3-8B-it scores 44%. Both models perform identically on ARC and MBPP, each scoring 60%. On LC AlpacaEval-2, Ours (Iterative RLHF) scores 32% versus LLaMA-3-8B-it’s 23%; on MT-Bench (×5), Ours (Iterative RLHF) achieves 42% compared to LLaMA-3-8B-it’s 40%. Finally, on Chat-Arena-Hard, both models underperform, with Ours (Iterative RLHF) at 29% and LLaMA-3-8B-it at 21%. The chart visually emphasizes that while performance varies by benchmark, Ours (Iterative RLHF) consistently matches or exceeds LLaMA-3-8B-it, particularly in HumanEval, TruthfulQA, LC AlpacaEval-2, and Chat-Arena-Hard, suggesting broader generalization and robustness in practical and challenging settings.
